decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - (a) Any advertisement displayed and any site used for the display of advertisements shall be retained in a clean and tidy condition to the reasonable satisfaction of the local planning authority. 
(b) Any structure or hoarding erected or used principally for the purpose of displaying advertisements shall be maintained in a safe condition. 
(c) Where an advertisement is required under these Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisement) (England) Regulations 2007 to be removed, the removal shall be carried out to the reasonable satisfaction of the local planning authority. 
(d) No advertisement shall be displayed without the permission of the owner of the site or any other person with an interest in the site entitled to grant permission. 
(e) No advertisement shall be sited or displayed so as to obscure or hinder the ready interpretation of any road traffic sign, railway signal or aid to navigation by water or air, or so as otherwise to render hazardous the use of any highway, railway, waterway or aerodrome (civil or military).
Reason: To comply with Regulation 14(1) and Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisement) (England) Regulations 2007 and to comply with paragraph 141 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Condition : 2 - This consent is for a limited period. This consent shall expire on 9th November 2026 and the advertisement hereby approved shall be removed and the land reinstated to its former condition by that date. 
Reason: The advertisement is only acceptable for a limited period, having regard to the amenity of the area in accordance with  policy LP9 of the Local Plan and the requirements of paragraph 141 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Condition : 3 - The maximum steady brightness of the sign hereby permitted is not to exceed 400 candelas per sq.m.
Reason: To ensure the sign does not have an adverse effect on the amenity of the area in accordance with Council policy LP9 of the Local Plan and to comply with paragraph 141 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Condition : 4 - The illumination of the sign(s) hereby permitted shall be by static illumination only. 
Reason: In the interest of highway safety and of the visual amenities of the locality in accordance with Council policy LP9 of the Local Plan and to comply with paragraph 141 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Condition : 5 - INFORMATIVE: This advertisement has been granted consent for a temporary period only. It is not considered that a permanent advert would be appropriate in this location for the reasons set out in the Officers Report. If any subsequent applications for advertisement consent were submitted for this advertisement following this consent lapsing, they would be unlikely to be approved on the basis that the advert would establish a degree of permanency that would harm visual amenity and the significance of heritage assets.

Reason : 1 - By reason of its design, siting and degree of permanence associated with this being the fourth application for temporary consent for the same advertisement, it is considered that the proposed advertisement would appear as a detracting and incongruous element in the street scene, detracting from historic views and the appreciation of adjacent Grade II Listed buildings. The proposal would therefore cause less than substantial harm to the significance of the Wandsworth Town Conservation Area and less than substantial harm to the setting of the adjacent Grade II Listed buildings. There are not considered to be any public benefits of the proposal that would outweigh this harm, contrary to London Plan Policy: HC1, Local Plan Policies: LP3 and LP9, Sections 66 (1) and Section 72(1) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 and Paragraphs 200 and 201 of the NPPF.

Reason : 2 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan consisting of the Core Strategy, Development Management Policies Document, Supplementary Planning documents and where appropriate the Site Specific Allocations Document as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the principle of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
description: Display of scaffold mounted externally illuminated shroud advertisement hoarding for a temporary period up until 09/11/2026
